title: Tracing probe harmonizer and anomaly veil for decoupled SLO ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Current SLO and burn-rate alerts rely on metric derivations that are partially coupled to tracing ingestion. We see mismatches between span-derived latency SLIs and metrics pipeline aggregates when sampling or enrichment pipelines change, which causes noisy burn-rate alerts and paging for infra and runtime teams. Goal: Build a lightweight "tracing probe harmonizer" that emits canonical SLI time-series from selected trace samples and a downstream "anomaly veil" layer that suppresses low-confidence burn-rate alerts while preserving high-fidelity paging. The harmonizer will: (1) normalize span attributes (service, route, model_variant, seq_len_bucket), (2) compute per-route p95/p99 latency SLIs and error-rate SLIs at ingestion time, and (3) emit a compact, labeled metric stream to the SLO pipeline. The anomaly veil will: (1) score alert signals for confidence using cross-signal correlation (trace metric agreement + request rate), (2) annotate alerts with confidence and suggested remediation tags, and (3) apply suppression rules for low-confidence spikes to reduce unnecessary pages. This ticket covers design, prototyping, and an initial canary rollout in us-west-2 on a subset of services (runtime, router, cache).
acceptance_criteria: Tracing harmonizer produces canonical SLI metrics for targeted routes with labels matching SLO definitions
New SLI series ingested into the SLO service with <= 2s additional ingestion latency and documented schema
Anomaly veil reduces pages from runtime false-positive burn-rate alerts by >= 40% during a 2-week canary without increasing missed incidents
Alert annotations include confidence score, top-2 contributing signals, and suggested fallback policies
E2E test and simulation harness available and run in CI; PRs reviewed and merged
implementation_notes: Component breakdown: (A) Harmonizer sidecar runs in tracing-ingest pipeline (Go) and uses a configurable probe list (service + route pattern). It enriches spans with normalized labels and computes rolling quantiles using t-digest. Output is emitted to metrics-kafka topic 'harmonized-sli.v1' with compact label set. (B) Anomaly veil is a lightweight scoring service (Python) that subscribes to harmonized-sli and existing metric aggregates, runs correlation heuristics (Pearson + rate-weighted agreement), and writes alert decisions to alert-gateway with 'confidence' and 'veil_reason' fields. (C) Pager policy integration: alerts with confidence < 0.6 go to a holding queue for automated retry or Slack-only notifications; >= 0.6 follow existing paging flows. Performance targets: harmonizer CPU < 5% per node, added 1-2ms per span at 99th. Backpressure behavior: harmonizer drops non-probe spans when memory pressure > 80% and emits drop metrics. Configuration: central config in SSM parameter store; canary flags for service list.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review + security review (1 week)
Phase 1: Prototype harmonizer on dev traces, validate SLI match vs batch metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Canary in us-west-2 for runtime and router (2 weeks) with shadow alerting enabled
Phase 3: Tune veil confidence thresholds and escalation rules (1 week)
Phase 4: Gradual expansion to other regions and services with metrics/QoS guardrails
risks_mitigation: Risk: Harmonizer mislabels spans causing SLO drift -> Mitigation: Strict schema tests + backcompat labels + opt-in via canary flag
Risk: Increased ingestion cost -> Mitigation: Probe whitelist and sampling cap; monitor cost metrics closely
Risk: Veil suppresses real incidents -> Mitigation: Shadow mode for 2 weeks + replay test harness to estimate false negative rate
Risk: Secret/config leakage for probe list -> Mitigation: store config in encrypted SSM and audit access
test_plan: Unit tests for t-digest quantile implementation and label normalization
Integration test: ingest synthetic trace corpus and verify harmonized-sli produced matches golden metrics
Simulation: run historical alert windows through veil to compute reduction in pages and any missed incidents
Canary monitoring: track pages, MTTD, MTTF for canary services vs baseline
